title: -4V_A: its level and the 5 V rail it needs
covers: section 3 (charge pump, -3.91 V to -4.05 V), decisions D-26, D-49 and D-51
summary: The charge pump runs from a 5 V rail that falls from 5.5 V to 3.6 V in 0.19 s. The rail feeds the pump through R30 with C21, as drawn. The pump is its averaged model: an inverter with the output resistance of the datasheet that keeps its output 2.7 % short of its supply at light load, and a regulator behind it. The load is the supply current of the amplifiers and the minimum load of the source regulator, once with that regulator at 0 V and once at 5 V. The run is repeated with the feedback reference and the 0.1 % divider at their limits, and once with a divider of 1 % parts, which is what the 0.1 % parts replaced.

notes: The pump is the averaged model. Its light-load level, 2.7 % short of the supply, is read from two figures of the datasheet (7-3 and 7-4) and is the figure that decides where the rail lets go; the datasheet does not state it in words or in its table.
The load on -4V_A is 5.1 mA of the amplifiers and the minimum load R69 of the source regulator: 3.1 mA with that regulator at 0 V and 6.9 mA at 5 V.
R30 is taken 1 % high. The capacitors lose capacitance under bias; no figure here depends on it.
